newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds in slow march to ANZAC Day.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds in slow march to ANZAC Day.

text.p: *Australian bond yields were kept to a narrow range during a much quieter morning session after Wednesday's sharp swings as the market squared up ahead of the long holiday weekend.
*Steady data stream next week both locally and in the U.S..
Australian bond yields were kept to a narrow range during a much quieter morning session after Wednesday's sharp swings as the market squared up ahead of the ANZAC Day long weekend.

Traders said the market was consolidating after falling sharply on profit-taking when the quarterly CPI report on Wednesday, which while still showing extremely subdued inflation, was not as weak as the market had been pricing in.
"The market looks to be holding up reasonably well now, but we're facing a big week next week for data, and the focus has switched to the U.S. to some extent," one trader said.

The market will get an idea of current economic activity next week with retail trade and building approvals for March due, along with the policy-sensitive average weekly ordinary time earnings report for the February quarter.

Another round of weak data could add to speculation, albeit minor at this stage, of a further easing in local rates given the low inflation outlook, this week's moderate low-pay award and the recent flow of data which show a patchy recovery.
Meanwhile, the U.S. faces first quarter GDP, the National Association of Purchasing Management Index and the key non-farm payrolls report.

The market still showed a slight underperforming bias against the dollar bloc after blowing out sharply on Wednesday's post-CPI sell-off. U.S. Treasuries held around New York's lower levels after the market lacked follow-through to a solidly bid five-year note auction.
